title: The Broken Pearl Necklace
devanagari: प्राप्तः षष्ठः सुकेश्या गणक दशमकः सङ्गृहीतः प्रियेण
दृष्टं षट्कं च सूत्रे कथय कतिपयैर्मौक्तिकैरेष हारः॥
translation: In a playful quarrel between lovers, a young woman's shining necklace of pearls broke. One third of the pearls fell to the floor, one fifth was seen on the bed, one sixth was found by the lovely-haired woman, and one tenth was gathered by her beloved. Six pearls were seen still on the string. O mathematician, tell me how many pearls the necklace had.
translation_hi: प्रेमियों की हँसी ठिठोली वाली नोक झोंक में एक युवती का मोतियों का चमकता हार टूट गया। उसका तीसरा भाग भूमि पर गिरा, पाँचवाँ भाग बिस्तर पर दिखा, छठा भाग सुंदर केशों वाली ने पाया और दसवाँ भाग प्रियतम ने उठा लिया। धागे में छह मोती बचे दिखे। हे गणितज्ञ, बताओ इस हार में कितने मोती थे?

words.note: Bright, sparkling. Visarga becomes स् before त: हारस्तारः.
Genitive of taruni. Hindi तरुण, तरुणी.
Genitive plural of mauktika (pearl). Hindi मोती comes from this.
Past participle of vi + √shri. -अः becomes -ओ before a voiced sound.
Past participle of pra + √ap. Hindi प्राप्त.
Past participle of sam + √grah. Hindi संग्रह.
Locative of sutra (thread). Hindi सूत, सूत्र.
Instrumental plural: 'made of how many pearls'.
Its visarga drops before a consonant: एष हारः.

grammar: Visarga before t: हारः + तारः → हारस्तारः. Before त/थ, visarga becomes स्.
-ah before a voiced sound: विशीर्णः + भूमौ → विशीर्णो भूमौ. Final -अः becomes -ओ before a voiced consonant.
Passive with instrumental: सुकेश्या प्राप्तः 'was found by the lovely-haired one', प्रियेण सङ्गृहीतः 'was gathered by the beloved'. The doer takes the instrumental case.
Fractions as ordinals: त्रिभाग, पञ्चमांश, षष्ठ, दशमक = 1/3, 1/5, 1/6, 1/10. 'The fifth' means 'the fifth part'.
question: How many pearls were in the necklace?
solution:
Let the pearls be x. The parts that fell: 1/3 + 1/5 + 1/6 + 1/10 = (10 + 6 + 5 + 3)/30 = 24/30

So the string keeps 6/30 of the pearls: (6/30) x = 6  ⟹  x = 30 pearls

Bhaskara's way, इष्टकर्म (ishta-karma, 'working with a chosen number'): guess any number, say 30. The parts leave 6 on the string. The verse also says 6, so the guess is exactly right.

Science link: ishta-karma is the method of false position: assume an answer, see how far off it is, then scale. Its descendant, regula falsi, is still taught in numerical methods for finding roots of equations.
